implement.name: Discipline — typed effects
implement.summary: An effect is a description of a value-producing action, not the action itself; the type carries that distinction

implement.name: Discipline — describe before execute
implement.summary: A function returns a description; execution happens at the seam, not at the call site

implement.name: Discipline — the effect boundary
implement.summary: The seam between description and execution is where the impure lives; nothing crosses it twice

implement.name: Discipline — service-locator avoided
implement.summary: The call site does not reach for the dependency it needs — environments and layers (where they apply) replace the constructor-injected service locator

implement.name: Approach — Result, when to use it
implement.summary: Result carries the success/failure pair through one operation; migrate to Either when two operations must compose on their failure

implement.name: Approach — Either<L, R>, the convention
implement.summary: Left is failure, right is success — never the other way, never a single type for both

implement.name: Approach — IO / suspend, the description/execution split
implement.summary: An IO is a description; execution happens at run; the keyword suspend names the discipline here, its behaviour lives in scrumia-kotlin

implement.name: Approach — effect.website, when to reach for the reference
implement.summary: effect.website is cited as the reference implementation for the typed-effect discipline; the environments and layers pattern lives here

implement.name: Error semantics — when to throw
implement.summary: Recoverable failures (validation, not-found, conflict, timeout) return a value; unrecoverable failures (invariant violation, exhausted resources, programmer error) throw

implement.name: Error semantics — retry as data, not marketing
implement.summary: A failure that may be retried carries Retry-After, attempt count, backoff hint; retry composes as a function on the effect, not as a try/catch loop at the call site

review.name: Discipline — a thrown exception a caller catches and continues
review.summary: If the caller catches the exception and continues, the failure was recoverable and the function should have returned a value, not thrown

review.name: Discipline — a try/catch loop retrying at the call site
review.summary: A loop around the call that retries on exception is retry as control flow, not retry as data — the failure does not carry the metadata the next attempt needs

review.name: Discipline — a call site that reaches for the dependency it needs
review.summary: A function reaching through a singleton, a global, or a parameter object for what it needs is the service-locator pattern the discipline refuses

review.name: Approach — Result, two operations composing on failure
review.summary: Composing two Result-returning operations on their failure channel needs Either — Result flattens one but not the other

review.name: Approach — Either, left as success or right as failure
review.summary: Either's left-for-failure convention is the rule; reversing it (or treating the type as a generic two-value carrier) is a finding against the rule

review.name: Approach — IO, executed at construction rather than at run
review.summary: An IO that performs its effect when constructed (rather than when run) is an IO in name only — the description/execution split is what the type buys

review.name: Approach — effect.website, an environment hand-wired at the call site
review.summary: An effect.website program that imports its services rather than declaring an environment has lost the layers mechanism the reference implementation ships for

find-spec.name: Effect discipline — the typed-effect lane
find-spec.summary: When a ticket or a review touches a function that produces, transforms, or consumes a side effect, this is the lane that owns the rule — discipline first, then the four approaches

find-spec.name: Effect discipline — dissociation from scrumia-ktor
find-spec.summary: HTTP-status-as-effect is owned by scrumia-ktor, not here — an error rule that names StatusCode or expectSuccess belongs there

find-spec.name: Effect discipline — dissociation from scrumia-kotlin
find-spec.summary: Rules on the behaviour of the suspend keyword or Flow live in scrumia-kotlin; here, suspend is named as the discipline's IO marker, never defined
